events.note: SOURCE=code | the plan assumed SCENARIO-01 shipped a `Result<Account, Failure>` vocabulary for use cases and the repository — actually SCENARIO-01 shipped `OpenAccountUseCase.open(accountNumber): Account` and `AccountRepository.findById(accountNumber): Account?`, so `DepositMoneyUseCase.deposit(accountNumber, amount): Account` was implemented against that and carries a non-null assertion on the lookup until SCENARIO-09 introduces not-found handling.

SOURCE=plan | the Structure & Contracts section puts the deposit action on the shared `AccountController`, which the test-designer's third note flags as contradicting `api-conventions` (one controller per business action, `DepositMoneyController`) — followed the plan and SCENARIO-01's precedent, so `AccountController` now has two actions.
SOURCE=plan | the plan places `Result<T, F>` in `application/Result.kt` while also
SOURCE=code | Structure & Contracts places `Result<T, F>` in `application/Result.kt` — actually at `domain/Result.kt`, since `Account` returns it and the domain may not import the application layer.

SOURCE=code | plan says to extract SCENARIO-03's positive-amount guard out of `deposit` into a shared private check — it was already extracted as `Account.isNotPositive(...)`; what actually needed sharing was the append-a-movement path, now a private `Account.record(kind, amount)` that both `deposit` and `withdraw` call.

SOURCE=code | rows 10, 11 and 13 name controller tests that already exist verbatim in `AccountControllerIT` for deposits (`returns_400_when_the_amount_is_missing`, `returns_400_when_the_amount_is_not_a_number`, `sends_a_zero_amount_to_the_use_case_instead_of_rejecting_it_at_the_boundary`) — duplicate method names in one class do not compile, so the withdrawal rows were renamed to say "withdrawal".

SOURCE=code | the Structure section says `Account.withdraw` "gains a second guard, checked after the existing positive-amount guard" — actually SCENARIO-04 implemented `withdraw` as a one-line delegation to a shared private `record(kind, amount)` that owns the positive-amount guard, so there was no withdrawal-only body to add a guard to; `withdraw` was given a body holding the balance guard alone, ahead of `record`.

SOURCE=code | the Structure section implies the controller's `refusal()` only needed extending once the mapping row was reached — actually `refusal()` is an exhaustive `when` over `AccountFailure`, so adding `InsufficientBalance` broke `compileKotlin` and coupled the use-case and controller batches into one batch-red run (the branch was stubbed with `TODO(...)` for that run only).

SOURCE=plan | Structure & Contracts put the OPENED filter and the most-recent-first reversal in the DTO mapper — the test-designer's note relocated both to `Account.statement()` in the domain, which is where rows 1–3 are written and where they were implemented; `StatementResponse.of` maps straight through.

SOURCE=plan | Structure & Contracts specified a `404` on the statement path when `findById` returns null — the test-designer's note defers it to SCENARIO-09, so the read path was left unguarded (`findById(...)!!`, consistent with `TransferMoneyUseCase`).

SOURCE=code | the plan assumed 4 `Account.reconstitute` call sites (`AccountTest` ×3, `AccountJpaAdapterIT` ×1) — actually there are 8 test call sites across 5 files (`AccountTest` ×2, `AccountJpaAdapterIT` ×1, `AccountControllerIT` ×3, `DepositMoneyUseCaseTest`/`WithdrawMoneyUseCaseTest`/`TransferMoneyUseCaseTest` ×1 each) plus `AccountJpaAdapter.toDomain`, because SCENARIO-06 and SCENARIO-07 added reconstitute-based fixtures the plan was written before. Handled by extracting one shared `anAccountWith(...)` fixture (`AccountFixtures.kt`) ahead of the signature change.

SOURCE=code | row 5's Contradiction assumed `AccountJpaAdapter.findById` "unwraps the decoded account unconditionally" — actually SCENARIO-01 implemented it as `accounts.findById(n).map(::toDomain).orElse(null)`, which already yields null once `toDomain` is nullable, so the row could not be made red for its stated reason.

SOURCE=plan | the plan recorded `findAll` as having "**no production caller** … test-only API surface until one exists" and accepted that — actually the Gherkin's "When the bank's accounts are read" names the caller, and the missing endpoint left the scenario unobservable outside the repository contract. `ListAccountsController` (`GET /accounts`) added in the review fix round, injecting `AccountRepository` directly, matching the statement seam the `arch-reviewer` passed as correct CQRS.
